archetypes.name: stub-isolation
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces PATH-injected mv and codex stubs that must delegate all non-target invocations to system binaries; missing delegation scope leaves later test cases contaminated.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the plan's PATH-stub design for mv (in review-and-fix tests) and the test-local codex wrapper (in check-reviewers tests) actually delegates every non-targeted invocation to the real system binary, and that the stub activation condition matches only the specific Codex auth-prep operation being tested. Check whether the plan specifies stub teardown (PATH restoration or subshell scope exit) before subsequent test cases run, and whether stub-introduced temp artifacts (captured config files, argv logs) fall inside the case-private TMPDIR so they cannot be seen by later cases. Confirm that the plan's described stub shape is consistent with equivalent stubs already present in skills/implement/scripts/test-codex-implementer.sh, since the plan says to mirror that file. Check whether the plan's narrowly targeted stub design would actually fail only the intended Codex auth-prep rename and not collide with harness-internal mv calls used for fixture setup. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: env-leak
archetypes.rationale: Many proposed cases set HOME, OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_HOME, and TMPDIR in incompatible combinations; unscoped exports produce cross-case false-green or false-red results.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each new test case proposed in the plan (check-reviewers t6/t7/t7a/t9/t10/legacy-strip/stamp-isolation, review-and-fix login-auth-prep-failure/login-fallback/env-key-auth-prep-failure/env-key-dispatch-failure, implementer cleanup), verify that every environment variable set for that case is either inside a subshell so it cannot escape, or explicitly unset or restored after the case ends. Pay particular attention to OPENAI_API_KEY and HOME, which the plan alternates between set and unset across cases and which the existing harness may export globally into subsequent test functions. Check whether any case implicitly relies on a previous case's HOME fixture without resetting it, creating a hidden ordering dependency that breaks on isolated runs. Confirm the plan's stamp-isolation checks (env-key probe writes only env-key stamp, login probe writes only login stamp) are scoped to private TMPDIRs and cannot see stamps written by earlier cases in the same run. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: assertion-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: Count-based, adjacency, and sentinel-absence assertions in the plan are vacuous if the artifact being asserted was never written or was written outside the capture scope.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each new assertion in the plan, verify that the artifact it reads (argv capture file, wrapper log, sidecar, TMPDIR snapshot, grep count) is guaranteed to be written before the assertion runs given the proposed execution order. Specifically check: the grep -Fxc count assertions on strip-edge-config.toml require the fixture to have been processed by the production strip path, not merely copied verbatim; the argv-adjacency proof for trusted-project -c requires a Codex probe to actually execute rather than short-circuit on a stamp hit; and sentinel-absent assertions require the capture file to exist so grep returns 0 rather than failing with a file-not-found exit that could be masked by || true. Check whether the plan's mutation-sanity instruction (flip one assertion per harness) is specific enough to catch vacuous assertions or only verifies assertion wiring. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
